_what: Settlement and reconciliation over a person's lists (src/list-settlements.mjs) as data: how an amount held by one row is applied across other rows, and how a set of cleared lines is closed against a statement. Every order, field name, limit and word is a row here; nothing in the engine names an invoice, a payment, a bank or any other business.
_scale: Amounts are added in whole units of 1/scale (cents for scale 100), so a total never drifts by a fraction.

orders.says: Rows with the earliest order value are settled first.
Rows with the latest order value are settled first.
Rows with the smallest open amount are settled first.
Rows with the largest open amount are settled first.

outcomes.some: {done} of {count} were done; the others are listed with why, and each can be tried again on its own.
outcomes.none: None of the {count} were done; each is listed with why.

words.no_row: The row {row_id} is not in the list {list_id}.
words.no_amount: The row {row_id} in {list_id} has no {field_id} number, so it has nothing to settle. An empty amount is not zero.
words.no_order: The order {order} is not one of: {orders}.
words.order_needs_field: The order {order} sorts by a field, so targets.order_field names it.
words.too_large: The list {list_id} has more than {limit} rows to read for this answer. Narrow it with targets.row_ids so the answer is complete, not a guess.
words.too_many_items: At most {limit} items can be settled in one call.
words.bad_amount: An amount to settle is a number above zero; {amount} is not.
words.over_open: The row {row_id} has only {open} open, so {amount} cannot be applied to it.
words.over_available: Only {available} is left on the source, so {amount} cannot be applied.
words.not_this_source: The allocation {allocation_id} belongs to a different source row.
words.over_applied_after_write: Another change used up the open amount first, so this allocation was removed again.
words.lines_closed: The line {row_id} is already closed in {receipt}.
words.no_lines: Close needs at least one cleared line in row_ids.
words.residual_unexplained: The statement and the cleared lines differ by {difference}. Give residual_reason in words, or clear the right lines, before closing.
words.residual_mismatch: The explained residual {given} is not the difference {difference}.
words.nothing_to_undo: There is no closed reconciliation of {lines} to undo.
words.line_changed: The line changed after it was closed.
words.line_removed: The line was removed after it was closed.
words.close_conflict: A line was closed by someone else while this close ran, so nothing was closed.
words.entry_too_short: An entry has at least two lines.
words.entry_unbalanced: The lines add to {sum}, not zero, so nothing was posted.
words.entry_partial: Some lines of the entry {entry_id} exist and others do not. Nothing was added.
words.line_kind: The line {row_id} has the kind {kind}, which is not one of: {kinds}.
words.line_base: The percent line {row_id} must say its base in {field_id}: one of {bases}.
words.bad_basis: The basis {basis} is not one of: {bases}.

options.says: Accrual: each row counts on the date it is due, whether or not it was paid.
Cash: each amount counts on the date it was applied, and every one lists the allocation behind it.
Both bases are shown side by side, each named.

bases.says: Every line since the last subtotal.
Every line above, subtotals not counted twice.
